item.title: Easton, PA, warming center offers services during extreme cold
item.description: The wind chill in Easton, Pennsylvania, was below zero on Wednesday.

item.title: Remembering Christa McAuliffe, the first teacher in space, 40 years after the Challenger explosion
item.description: Forty years ago, the Challenger space shuttle exploded over Cape Canaveral, Florida, killing all seven crew members.

item.title: The restoration of a Revolutionary War gunboat underway at the Smithsonian
item.description: At the Battle of Valcour Island on Lake Champlain in the Revolutionary War, a gunboat called the Philadelphia for the colonies was sunk in battle.

item.title: Threats against politicians increase
item.description: Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar was sprayed with an unknown liquid at a town hall event in Minneapolis.

item.title: Mass. record-breaking auction of Bob Ross art pulls in over $1 million for public TV
item.description: Each painting up for auction Tuesday well exceeded their appraisals, with one breaking the record for a Bob Ross piece sold at auction. The proceeds of the blockbuster sale will go toward Create, a network run American Public Television, the original distributors of Ross' show "The Joy of Painting."

item.title: Healey's new $63 billion budget, up 3.8%, would eliminate coverage for weight loss drugs
item.description: Healey’s spending plan comes as state revenues are growing. But her administration is contending with an uncertain economic outlook, a president who’s increasingly hostile toward Democratic states and a rising rate of spending that fiscal hawks warn is unsustainable.

item.title: Mass. will spend millions to comply with Trump's health policies
item.description: Officials told WBUR they expect the bulk of the new costs, about $21 million, will go toward upgrading computer systems needed to determine who is eligible for Medicaid.

item.title: Boston's Museum of Fine Arts announces layoffs
item.description: The museum notified employees of the layoffs in an internal email sent Tuesday. More than 30 museum positions will be affected.

item.title: How Minneapolis is standing up to ICE
item.description: In Minneapolis, grassroots groups have sprung into action against ICE. They’re protesting, running workshops on constitutional rights, and delivering groceries to people afraid of leaving their homes.

item.title: ICE operations in Maine are taking an emotional toll on the family and friends of those detained
item.description: ICE says its made than 200 arrests in Maine since expending operations in the state last week. And while the agency has said it's going after criminals, many of those detained are asylum seekers with no criminal records, according to their lawyers, family members and employers.
